# kernel

> Apply a one-dimensional strided array function to an input ndarray according to a callback function using linear view iteration.

<section class="intro">

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var kernel = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/base/kernels/generic/nullary-strided1d-by/linear' );
```

<!-- lint disable maximum-heading-length -->

#### kernel( fcn, arrays, ref, views, shape, stridesX, strategyX, ibuf, ldims, cdims, options, hasOpts, clbk, thisArg )

<!-- lint enable maximum-heading-length -->

Applies a one-dimensional strided array function to an input ndarray according to a callback function using linear view iteration.

<!-- eslint-disable max-len -->

```javascript
var Float64Array = require( '@stdlib/array/float64' );
var ndarray2array = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/base/to-array' );
var zeros = require( '@stdlib/array/base/zeros' );
var gfillBy = require( '@stdlib/blas/ext/base/ndarray/gfill-by' );
var strategy = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/base/kernels/generic/unary-strided1d/strategy' );

function clbk( value, idx ) {
    return ( idx[ 1 ]*100 ) + ( idx[ 2 ]*10 ) + idx[ 3 ];
}

// Create a data buffer:
var xbuf = new Float64Array( 12 );

// Define the array shape:
var xsh = [ 1, 3, 2, 2 ];

// Define the array strides:
var sx = [ 12, 4, 2, 1 ];

// Define the index offset:
var ox = 0;

// Create an input ndarray descriptor:
var x = {
    'dtype': 'float64',
    'data': xbuf,
    'shape': xsh,
    'strides': sx,
    'offset': ox,
    'order': 'row-major'
};

// Create an ndarray descriptor for the starting index (inclusive):
var start = {
    'dtype': 'float64',
    'data': new Float64Array( [ 0.0 ] ),
    'shape': [ 1, 3 ],
    'strides': [ 0, 0 ],
    'offset': 0,
    'order': 'row-major'
};

// Create an ndarray descriptor for the ending index (exclusive):
var end = {
    'dtype': 'float64',
    'data': new Float64Array( [ 4.0 ] ),
    'shape': [ 1, 3 ],
    'strides': [ 0, 0 ],
    'offset': 0,
    'order': 'row-major'
};

// Initialize ndarray descriptors representing subarray views:
var views = [
    {
        'dtype': x.dtype,
        'data': x.data,
        'shape': [ 2, 2 ],
        'strides': [ 2, 1 ],
        'offset': x.offset,
        'order': x.order
    },
    {
        'dtype': start.dtype,
        'data': start.data,
        'shape': [],
        'strides': [ 0 ],
        'offset': start.offset,
        'order': start.order
    },
    {
        'dtype': end.dtype,
        'data': end.data,
        'shape': [],
        'strides': [ 0 ],
        'offset': end.offset,
        'order': end.order
    }
];

// Resolve an input strategy when iterating over subarray views:
var strategyX = strategy( views[ 0 ] );

// Create a workspace array for storing iteration indices:
var ibuf = zeros( xsh.length );

// Define the loop and core dimensions:
var ldims = [ 0, 1 ];
var cdims = [ 2, 3 ];

// Apply strided function:
kernel( gfillBy, [ x, start, end ], x, views, [ 1, 3 ], [ 12, 4 ], strategyX, ibuf, ldims, cdims, {}, false, clbk, {} );

var arr = ndarray2array( x.data, x.shape, x.strides, x.offset, x.order );
// returns [ [ [ [ 0.0, 1.0 ], [ 10.0, 11.0 ] ], [ [ 100.0, 101.0 ], [ 110.0, 111.0 ] ], [ [ 200.0, 201.0 ], [ 210.0, 211.0 ] ] ] ]
```

The function has the following parameters:

-   **fcn**: function which will be applied to a one-dimensional input subarray according to a callback function.
-   **arrays**: array containing an input ndarray [descriptor][@stdlib/ndarray/base/descriptor], followed by any additional ndarray arguments.
-   **ref**: original input ndarray provided to a callback function.
-   **views**: initialized ndarray [descriptors][@stdlib/ndarray/base/descriptor] representing subarray views.
-   **shape**: loop dimensions.
-   **stridesX**: loop dimension strides for the input ndarray.
-   **strategyX**: strategy for marshaling data to and from an input ndarray view.
-   **ibuf**: workspace for storing iteration indices.
-   **ldims**: list of loop dimensions.
-   **cdims**: list of "core" dimensions.
-   **options**: function options which are passed through to `fcn`.
-   **hasOpts**: boolean indicating whether to pass an options argument to a strided array function.
-   **clbk**: callback function.
-   **thisArg**: callback execution context.

The function iterates based on the linear **view** index, regardless as to how the data is stored in memory.

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   The strided array function is expected to have the following signature:

    ```text
    fcn( arrays[, options], clbk )
    ```

    where

    -   **arrays**: array containing a one-dimensional subarray of the input ndarray and any additional ndarray arguments as subarrays.
    -   **options**: function options (_optional_).
    -   **clbk**: callback function.

-   The callback function is provided the following arguments:

    -   **value**: current array element.
    -   **idx**: current array element indices.
    -   **arr**: the original input ndarray.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

<!-- eslint-disable max-len -->

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

```javascript
var Float64Array = require( '@stdlib/array/float64' );
var ndarray2array = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/base/to-array' );
var zeros = require( '@stdlib/array/base/zeros' );
var gfillBy = require( '@stdlib/blas/ext/base/ndarray/gfill-by' );
var strategy = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/base/kernels/generic/unary-strided1d/strategy' );
var kernel = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/base/kernels/generic/nullary-strided1d-by/linear' );

function clbk( value, idx ) {
    return ( idx[ 2 ]*100 ) + ( idx[ 3 ]*10 ) + idx[ 4 ];
}

// Create a data buffer:
var xbuf = new Float64Array( 12 );

// Define the array shape:
var xsh = [ 1, 1, 3, 2, 2 ];

// Define the array strides:
var sx = [ 12, 12, 4, 2, 1 ];

// Define the index offset:
var ox = 0;

// Create an input ndarray descriptor:
var x = {
    'dtype': 'float64',
    'data': xbuf,
    'shape': xsh,
    'strides': sx,
    'offset': ox,
    'order': 'row-major'
};

// Create an ndarray descriptor for the starting index (inclusive):
var start = {
    'dtype': 'float64',
    'data': new Float64Array( [ 0.0 ] ),
    'shape': [ 1, 1, 3 ],
    'strides': [ 0, 0, 0 ],
    'offset': 0,
    'order': 'row-major'
};

// Create an ndarray descriptor for the ending index (exclusive):
var end = {
    'dtype': 'float64',
    'data': new Float64Array( [ 4.0 ] ),
    'shape': [ 1, 1, 3 ],
    'strides': [ 0, 0, 0 ],
    'offset': 0,
    'order': 'row-major'
};

// Initialize ndarray descriptors representing subarray views:
var views = [
    {
        'dtype': x.dtype,
        'data': x.data,
        'shape': [ 2, 2 ],
        'strides': [ 2, 1 ],
        'offset': x.offset,
        'order': x.order
    },
    {
        'dtype': start.dtype,
        'data': start.data,
        'shape': [],
        'strides': [ 0 ],
        'offset': start.offset,
        'order': start.order
    },
    {
        'dtype': end.dtype,
        'data': end.data,
        'shape': [],
        'strides': [ 0 ],
        'offset': end.offset,
        'order': end.order
    }
];

// Resolve an input strategy when iterating over subarray views:
var strategyX = strategy( views[ 0 ] );

// Create a workspace array for storing iteration indices:
var ibuf = zeros( xsh.length );

// Define the loop and core dimensions:
var ldims = [ 0, 1, 2 ];
var cdims = [ 3, 4 ];

// Apply strided function:
kernel( gfillBy, [ x, start, end ], x, views, [ 1, 1, 3 ], [ 12, 12, 4 ], strategyX, ibuf, ldims, cdims, {}, false, clbk, {} );

console.log( ndarray2array( x.data, x.shape, x.strides, x.offset, x.order ) );
```

</section>
